conventions.beats_per_measure: unbounded — measure width is derived from content (schema v2 §9.1)
conventions.feel: swing and shuffle are MARKED in tab.feel, never written out as triplet pairs (§2.5). Bossa is `straight` — even-eighth music whose groove is syncopation, not a subdivision ratio. A tab carrying feel=swing AND literal triplet durations is double-applied swing and fails V9.

songs.title: A Horse with No Name
songs.passage: Verse — the entire song alternates two chords; 8 bars = two full cycles.
songs.why_in_set: Two chords, both open position, no articulation. The cleanest possible test that the generator can spell a minor tonic.
songs.mode_flip_guard: Em must contain G natural. A G# here is the T1 defect.

songs.title: Zombie
songs.passage: Verse/chorus loop — Em C G D/F#, one bar each, twice.
songs.why_in_set: The canonical i-VI-III-VII minor loop. Four chords, every third present, nothing to articulate.
songs.mode_flip_guard: Em needs G natural; D/F# needs F# in the bass AND as a third.
cannot_verify: Whether the recorded voicing is D/F# or plain D. Both are correct harmony; the bass note is an arrangement detail. Scored as D major either way.

songs.title: Ain't No Sunshine
songs.passage: Verse — Am Em7 G Am, one bar each, twice.
songs.why_in_set: A minor tonic with a m7 on the v. Tests the third on two different minor chords in one passage.
songs.mode_flip_guard: Am must contain C natural, not C#. Em7 must contain G natural and D.
cannot_verify: This is not a guitar record — the hook is strings and Withers' voice, and the guitar is a supporting part. The harmony is certain; whether it should be TAUGHT as a guitar song is a curation call, not a tab question. Flagged for Junie/Nadia.

songs.title: Canon in D
songs.passage: The ground bass cycle — D A Bm F#m G D G A, one bar each. 8 bars is exactly one full cycle.
songs.why_in_set: Public domain (migration 0015 tags it so), and the only song in the set whose 8-bar excerpt is a COMPLETE musical unit rather than a slice. Two barre minors test position.
songs.mode_flip_guard: Bm needs D natural; F#m needs A natural. Both are barre shapes, so a one-fret position error (T3) changes the chord.

songs.title: Autumn Leaves
songs.feel: medium swing — comped on beats, not a melody line
songs.passage: A section, bars 1-8: ii-V-I in Bb then ii-V-i in Gm.
songs.why_in_set: The clearest ii-V-I in the catalog. Four chord qualities (m7, dom7, maj7, m7b5) in eight bars — nowhere to hide a missing third.
songs.mode_flip_guard: Am7b5 must contain Eb (the flat five). A natural E makes it Am7 and destroys the cadence.
cannot_verify: The swing RATIO is not notated, and that is deliberate: `tab_feel` is `swing`, so the player is told to swing the eighths and supplies the ratio from the 120 bpm marking (FLE-105 Q1). What is NOT here is a comping RHYTHM — these are quarter-note stabs on all four beats, which is correct as pitch and inert as time. A real medium-swing comp anticipates and leaves holes. FLE-107 re-notates this song; until it does, a player practising these eight bars from the screen gets the changes and not the groove.

songs.title: Take the 'A' Train
songs.why_in_set: The D7#11 is the whole identity of this tune. An altered dominant is the single hardest thing for the generator to get right, and it is checkable without a recording.
songs.mode_flip_guard: D7#11 must contain G# (the #11). Drop it and you have an ordinary D7, which is the wrong tune.

songs.title: Blue Bossa
songs.why_in_set: Minor ii-V-i. Pairs with Autumn Leaves as the same cadence a minor third away, so a generator that transposes a house pattern instead of transcribing (T7) shows up as an exact shape match between the two.
songs.mode_flip_guard: Cm7 needs Eb; Dm7b5 needs Ab; G7b9 needs B natural AND Ab. The b9 is the sound of the cadence.
cannot_verify: Charts vary between G7alt / G7b9 / G7#5 in bar 6. I committed G7b9. Any altered G dominant should score as correct; a plain G7 should not.

songs.title: The Girl from Ipanema
songs.why_in_set: The Gb7 in bar 6 is a tritone substitution — the one chord in the set that is not diatonic to anything. A generator guessing from the key signature cannot reach it.
songs.mode_flip_guard: Gb7 must contain Bb (= A#, its third). Gm7 and Gb7 sit one fret apart; a position slip (T3) swaps them.

songs.title: Hotel California
songs.passage: The 8-bar progression, one bar each: Bm F#7 A E G D Em F#7.
songs.why_in_set: The hardest mode-flip trap available without articulation. A minor key whose dominant is a MAJOR seventh chord — the generator must put A# over a B-minor tonality, which is exactly the move it gets backwards in the other direction (T1: major third where the minor belongs).
songs.mode_flip_guard: Bm needs D natural. F#7 needs A# — not A. Both in the same 8 bars, in opposite directions. Em needs G natural; E major needs G#, two bars apart.
cannot_verify: The recorded intro is a 12-string arrangement with the voicings spread across two guitars. I committed the single-guitar chord reading, which is the correct harmony and the standard way it is taught. A 6-string transcription cannot be note-for-note identical to the record here.

songs.title: Giant Steps
songs.key: modulating — B / G / Eb major thirds cycle
songs.passage: Bars 1-8: Bmaj7 D7 Gmaj7 Bb7 Ebmaj7 Ebmaj7 Am7 D7.
songs.why_in_set: The only song I can certify at the top of the difficulty range (see the writeup: above 0.65 this catalog is hard BECAUSE of articulation, which the schema drops). Three key centres in eight bars — no house pattern survives it.
songs.mode_flip_guard: Bmaj7 needs D# and A#. Gmaj7 needs F#. Ebmaj7 needs D. Each maj7 is a different key centre; a single borrowed scale produces wrong notes in two of the three.
cannot_verify: Bar 6 is Ebmaj7 held for two bars in the common chart; some fake books split it. Harmonically identical, so either should score as correct.

songs.title: Wonderwall
songs.key: E minor shapes — sounds F# minor with the capo at 2
songs.passage: Verse — Em7 G Dsus4 A7sus4, one bar each, twice.
songs.why_in_set: The song the original ten could not hold: it was excluded ONLY because there was no capo field, and §7 added one. It is also the lowest-barrier rock song in the catalog, so it anchors the bottom of the window with something the roster actually asked for.
songs.mode_flip_guard: Em7 needs G natural and D. The two sus chords must contain NO third at all — a Dsus4 with an F# in it is a D major chord and the suspension is the sound of the verse.
cannot_verify: The strum pattern. Nothing recording-side would help: the schema has no strum direction, so there is no way to write down down-down-up-up-down-up. The pitches and the capo position are what is committed; the right hand is not.

songs.title: Sweet Home Chicago
songs.feel: shuffle — the eighths are swung, hard
songs.passage: Bars 1-8 of the 12-bar form: I I I I IV IV I I, boogie figure on the two lowest strings.
songs.why_in_set: The most-played form in the music this roster plays, and the first song in the set whose material is a FIGURE rather than a chord sequence. It is also the pair to Folsom Prison Blues on purpose: identical harmony, opposite feel, so a player meets shuffle and straight over the same changes.
songs.mode_flip_guard: No third anywhere in this figure, in either direction. The b7 (D) must be present — it is what makes this a blues rather than a rock fifth — and a G# or G natural appearing here is wrong.
cannot_verify: Whether the form takes the quick change (bar 2 to the IV). Both readings are standard; this commits the straight four bars of I. It is a product decision about which reading we teach, not a question about the record.

Johnson's own 1936 solo performance, note for note. What is committed is the standard BAND reading — the electric arrangement every blues player means by this title. Johnson's is a fingerpicked country-blues part and a different guitar part entirely; the catalog credits him, and which of the two Fletcher teaches is Junie's call.

songs.title: Folsom Prison Blues
songs.feel: straight — boom-chick, bass note then strum
songs.passage: The complete 12-bar form: I I I I IV IV I I V V I I.
songs.why_in_set: The only song in the set other than Canon in D whose excerpt is a COMPLETE musical unit rather than a slice — all twelve bars, so the V actually arrives. Bars 1-8 of a 12-bar never reach the dominant, which means the eight-bar convention had been quietly hiding the chord that resolves the form.
songs.mode_flip_guard: B7 must contain D# (its third) and A (its b7). Flatten the D# to D and the V stops being a dominant, which is the one chord in a 12-bar that cannot be fudged.
cannot_verify: WHICH RECORDING. This is the 1955 Sun reading, in E. The 1968 Folsom Prison live version is a tone higher and is the one most people have heard. The 12-bar harmony is identical either way, so a player practising this learns the right thing; the absolute key is the only thing at stake, and I am not going to assert one from memory.

The boom-chick itself. These are quarter-note chord stabs, so what is committed is the harmony and the form, not Luther Perkins' alternating bass-and-strum — which is most of what the song SOUNDS like. Same class of gap as the swing comping on Autumn Leaves.

songs.title: Pride and Joy
songs.key: E shapes — sounds Eb, tuned down a semitone
songs.feel: shuffle — a Texas shuffle, swung hard
songs.passage: Bars 1-8 of the 12-bar form: I I I I IV IV I I, the shuffle bass figure.
songs.why_in_set: It puts a blues at 0.64, in the band where the set was all jazz standards, and it is the one song here whose tuning makes the shape and sounding frames differ — so it is the only end-to-end evidence that a down-tuned song is checked in the right frame rather than scored a semitone flat across the board.
songs.mode_flip_guard: Same as Sweet Home Chicago, one semitone down: no third, b7 present. In the SOUNDING frame that is Eb-Bb-C-Db, so a checker that forgets the tuning will read every note of it as foreign.
cannot_verify: SRV's upper-voice fills, the rake, and the double-stop bends. What is committed is the bass figure only. That is the honest half: the shuffle under the song is this, and everything above it is the part I would need the record and a reference transcription to write.

NOTE, not a caveat about the record: these eight bars are IDENTICAL to Sweet Home Chicago's, note for note, because the figure genuinely is the same one — the differences are the tuning, the tempo and the fills I did not commit. That is a real fact about the music and a real curation problem: two pilot days could serve what looks like the same screen. Flagged for Nadia to sequence, not to be fixed by inventing a difference.

songs.title: Sultans of Swing
songs.passage: Intro, bars 1-8: Dm C Bb A, one bar each, twice.
songs.why_in_set: The top of the window a pilot user can actually reach. With player_level capped at 0.70 the highest window is 0.55-0.85, and before this the only rock in it was Hotel California. It also carries the mode flip pointing the OTHER way — the fourth chord of a D minor tune is A MAJOR.
songs.mode_flip_guard: A must contain C# — a natural C makes it Am and the turnaround loses its pull. This is the reverse of FLE-102's T1 (a major third where a minor belonged), so a generator patched to 'use the natural minor in a minor key' fails exactly here.
cannot_verify: Knopfler's arpeggiation figure and his fills, note for note. The harmony Dm-C-Bb-A is not in dispute and is what is committed; the fingerpicked pattern that makes it sound like this record is not, and would need the record plus a reference transcription.
